chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When the dog touches your garment, if it was dry then sprinkle it, and if it was wet then wash it.
ai.seo_question: How to purify clothes after a dog touches them according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the specific jurisprudence of *taharah* regarding canine contact, distinguishing between dry and wet states to determine the requisite purification method. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition where 'sprinkling' (*tanazzuh*) is often interpreted as a lighter form of cleansing for dry contact, contrasting with the full washing (*ghasl*) required for wet contact, a nuance central to discussions on the purity of the dog's body versus its saliva.
